newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then slips after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then slips after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by short covering and firmer physical prices, ended higher Wednesday in moderate activity, then slipped in after-hours trade on a slightly bearish inventory report.

June rallied 8.7 cents to close at $2.276 per million British thermal units, then slipped on ACCESS to the $2.25 area after the AGA data. July settled 6.6 cents higher at $2.275. Other months ended up by 2.9 to 5.9 cents.
"Cash was pretty strong today, but we're coming off now after the AGAs. It wasn't that bearish but it was at the high end of the (expected) range," said one East Coast trader.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 70 bcf and were still 216 bcf, or 29 percent, over year-ago levels. Eastern storage, which gained 40 bcf last week, was 121 bcf, or 39 percent, above 1996 levels. A Reuter poll earlier showed most expected a 60-70 bcf weekly stock build.

While some expected steady heat in the Southwest and stepped up injections to keep the market relatively firm near-term, others focused on milder forecasts for the rest of the nation that promised only limited cooling or heating demand.
Technically, traders pegged June resistance at $2.30 and then at contract high of $2.43. Support was seen at $2.14-2.15, with major buying expected at $2.05.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed a few cents Wednesday to about the $2.20 level. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas edged up slightly to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip jumped five cents to $2.283. NYMEX said 33,974 contracts traded, up slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 30,565.

On the KCBT, June finished 7.4 cents higher at $2.10, while deferreds ended up by 3.5 to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.3 cents to 17.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 284 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's total of 333.
